headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: Gemini CLI can write shared files and gpt-researcher can ingest them, while both use broad network egress and overlapping MCP/API surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Gemini CLI can read/write the filesystem and use MCP; gpt-researcher reads local documents and also calls MCP/APIs. A shared workspace creates a plausible instruction-injection bridge if one agent writes attacker-controlled content that the other later parses as trusted input. This is not provably blocked, but it is not a default direct channel either.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory or document set, injected instructions can cross from A to B.
IF B treats A-produced files as authoritative prompts or task context, prompt injection becomes actionable.
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent.
Disable automatic ingestion of newly written files.
Require provenance tags on files before B reads them.
Use a read-only handoff directory for A→B transfers.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and prompt-boundary enforcement in the orchestrator.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Gemini CLI touches source code, cwd files, and shell environment, and can egress broadly; gpt-researcher reads local documents and sends queries/reports through multiple APIs. If they share a workspace, sensitive files handled by A can be exposed through B's outbound API calls. The blast radius includes source code and secrets, so this is dangerous by default once co-located.
conditions: IF A and B share a directory containing secrets or proprietary code, B can transmit that content to third-party services.
IF B is configured to summarize or upload local documents, leakage extends beyond one file.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared workspace.
Run B on a scrubbed copy of inputs only.
Disable API-backed document ingestion for sensitive folders.
Rotate any credentials present in the shared cwd.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write or mutate shared state: Gemini CLI explicitly modifies git state and filesystem, while gpt-researcher reads local documents and can run subprocesses with broad network egress. The profiles indicate shared state via filesystem and git only, so concurrent writes to the same repo can race and corrupt work or commits. No locking is documented, so the conflict is severe.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git repository, commit races or overwrite conflicts can occur.
IF B writes generated artifacts into the same directory A edits, last-writer-wins corruption is possible.
mitigations: Assign separate branches per agent.
Use a lockfile around git operations.
Make one agent read-only.
Stage outputs in per-agent subdirectories.
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Gemini CLI can produce code, shell actions, and MCP-driven outputs; gpt-researcher has planner/execution/publisher roles and can turn research outputs into reports. If B consumes A's output without verification, A's mistakes or fabricated facts can cascade into published research or downstream actions. The pair lacks a documented verification boundary, so the default pathway is risky.
conditions: IF B uses A-generated text as source material without independent checks, errors propagate into reports.
IF A emits malformed citations or code snippets that B republishes, downstream consumers inherit the mistake.
mitigations: Require source verification before publication.
Insert a human review step for A→B handoffs.
Have B cite only primary sources, not A summaries.
Mark A outputs as untrusted in the orchestrator.
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking and citation validation.

E_compliance.rationale: Gemini CLI handles shell environment and files in cwd, while gpt-researcher processes local documents and sends them to multiple external APIs. If regulated data such as EU PII or confidential documents enters the shared workspace, the pair can create a residency/retention mismatch because B's API-backed workflow may export it outside local control. The profiles do not prove a specific legal violation, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is placed in the shared workspace, B may transmit it to external services.
IF retention requirements require local-only processing, B's API-backed workflow violates that constraint.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared workspace.
Use synthetic or redacted documents for B.
Disable external API calls for sensitive runs.
Document a data-processing agreement before use.
requires-engineering: implement residency-aware routing and retention controls.
